subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to Personally Identifiable Information (PII) training questions — identify what counts as PII and how to protect it, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: PII Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Personally Identifiable Information (PII) quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Safeguarding, breach reporting, and PII vs. PHI.
whyItWorks: PII questions often hinge on whether a specific piece of information counts as PII on its own or only in combination with other data — a distinction that's easy to second-guess. Cambo reads the exact scenario and explains the reasoning, not just the answer.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following, standing alone, is generally considered PII?
options: A job title
A ZIP code
A Social Security Number
A company department name
sampleQuestions.a: A Social Security Number — it can identify a specific individual on its own, unlike a first name or job title alone.

sampleQuestions.q: What should you do if you discover a PII breach?
options: Report it immediately through your organization's established breach reporting procedure, often within one hour
Wait until you can confirm how many records were affected
Delete the affected records to limit the exposure
Notify the affected individuals directly before telling anyone else
sampleQuestions.a: Report it immediately through your organization's established breach reporting procedure — most policies require reporting within a strict time window, often one hour.

sampleQuestions.q: Is a person's job title alone generally considered PII?
options: Yes — any workplace attribute is PII on its own
No — a job title alone usually doesn't identify a specific individual; it becomes a concern combined with other identifying details
Yes — but only for personnel in supervisory roles
No — job titles are never a PII concern in any combination
sampleQuestions.a: No — a job title by itself usually doesn't identify a specific individual. It becomes a PII concern only when combined with other identifying details, like a full name.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the difference between PII and "sensitive PII"?
options: Sensitive PII refers only to medical information; PII covers everything else
Sensitive PII is stored electronically, while PII is kept on paper
Sensitive PII is a subset that could cause substantial harm if exposed — such as an SSN, financial account number, or biometric data — and requires stricter safeguards
There is no practical difference; the terms are used interchangeably
sampleQuestions.a: Sensitive PII is a subset that could cause substantial harm if exposed — like an SSN, financial account number, or biometric data — and typically requires stricter safeguards than PII in general.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the general rule for emailing PII to a personal email account?
options: It is permitted if the file is password protected
It is permitted when working remotely
It is permitted if the employee deletes the message afterward
It is prohibited — PII must stay within authorized government or organizational systems
sampleQuestions.a: It's prohibited — PII should stay within authorized government or organizational systems, and sending it to a personal account is one of the most common PII-handling violations covered in training.

sampleQuestions.q: Why does PII training cover disposal procedures, not just storage and transmission?
options: Because improperly discarded documents and unwiped devices are a real source of breaches, so protection must cover the entire data lifecycle
Because disposal is the only stage regulated by federal law
Because retention schedules require destroying all records annually
Because disposal costs are a significant part of most agency budgets
sampleQuestions.a: Because improperly discarded documents or devices (like an unshredded printout or an unwiped hard drive) are a real-world source of PII breaches — protection has to extend through the entire data lifecycle.

faqs.q: How often is PII training required?
faqs.a: Annually for most DoD and federal personnel with access to systems or records containing PII.

faqs.q: What's the difference between PII and PHI?
faqs.a: PII is any information that can identify a specific individual. PHI (Protected Health Information) is a subset of PII specifically tied to health records and covered under HIPAA.
Anyone who collects, accesses, maintains, or disposes of records containing personally identifiable information as part of their job.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or any official PII program?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense.
Full name combined with SSN, date of birth, driver's license number, financial account numbers, or biometric records — generally anything that can identify or be traced to a specific individual.

faqs.q: What happens if PII is mishandled?
faqs.a: Consequences range from required breach reporting and mitigation to disciplinary action, depending on the severity and whether the mishandling was negligent or intentional.
